sections.heading: The Keyword Matching Revolution: From Boolean to Semantic Vector Space
sections.content:
For most of the past decade, ATS keyword matching operated on a simple boolean principle: either the resume contained the exact word or phrase, or it didn't. In 2026, that approach is obsolete.

Modern ATS platforms — including SmartRecruiters, Greenhouse, Lever, and Workday — have adopted transformer-based embedding models that semantically score your resume. This means a resume discussing "automated CI/CD deployments" will score well against a job description that mentions "GitHub Actions" — because the embedding vectors are close in semantic space.

Industry research note (2026): A 2026 analysis of 1,000+ tech resumes found that exact-match-only strategies still produce passing ATS scores of 62–68% on legacy systems, but only 34–41% on embedding-capable ATS systems. CVCircle's Lexical Density Engine tests against both paradigms.

sections.content:

  13. ATS Template Span: CVCircle's ENGINEERING PRO and DATA ANALYST PRO templates validated at 98/100 on 20 ATS platforms

sections.heading: How Many Keywords Is Too Many? Avoiding ATS Penalties for Over-Optimisation
sections.content:
While keywords are essential, overuse triggers penalties in modern ATS scoring engines. CVCircle's Lexical Density Engine applies diminishing returns beyond the optimal keyword threshold, and excessive repetition results in a lower overall score despite high keyword density.

Optimal Keyword Density by Section

  • Professional Summary: Target 4–6 top-priority keywords; density ~8–12%
  • Technical Skills: Target 15–20 skills; density as clear categorical listing
  • Experience bullets: Each bullet should contain 1–2 context-relevant keywords; don't force-more
  • Avoid: Keyword stuffing more than 3 repetitions of the same keyword per resume

❌ Over-optimised Resume Warning

Writing “Python, Python, and Python” three times to improve keyword match score will actually LOWER your Lexical Density Score via repetition-penalty.

✅ CVCircle AI Score Update

The real-time scorebubble reflects the penalty immediately — once you repeat a keyword more than twice, the scorebar drops, not rises.
